intro.opening: Roughly three and a half hours south of Aswan, on the desert road to Sudan, the road descends, the water draws close, and Abu Simbel appears: two temples cut directly into a sandstone cliff, their four colossal seated figures of Ramses II staring across Lake Nasser. This is a long day, and the drive is not particularly scenic. None of that diminishes what you find when you get there.
intro.whyThisOrder: Departure is early, typically around 4 a.m., because the Egyptian authorities organise road travel to Abu Simbel in escorted convoys, and the timing is fixed by that schedule rather than preference. Arriving early matters: by mid-morning tour buses from across Upper Egypt have arrived and the temple interiors fill quickly, and the sun can be punishing by late morning. Because the tour is private, the pace at the temples is yours to set.
intro.returnNote: Back in Aswan typically late afternoon, depending on departure time and any stops along the road

lunch.text: Included in the Base + Entrance Fees & Lunch tier only (a midday meal)

intro.closingLine: What you find at the end of that drive has no equivalent anywhere else in Egypt.

stops.title: Pickup from your Aswan hotel
stops.text: Departure is early, to coincide with convoy hours: the Egyptian authorities organise road travel to Abu Simbel in escorted groups. You travel in a private, air-conditioned vehicle.

stops.title: The road along Lake Nasser
stops.text: The road south runs along the western bank of Lake Nasser through open desert. It is a smooth, well-maintained highway, and the drive takes approximately three and a half hours.

stops.title: The Great Temple of Ramses II
stops.text: You reach Abu Simbel before the site becomes crowded, with time in the great hypostyle hall before the crowds press in. Four seated statues of Ramses II, each roughly twenty metres tall, flank the entrance. Inside are eight Osiride pillars, reliefs of the Battle of Kadesh, and the inner sanctuary that the sun reaches every 22 February and 22 October.
sites: Great Temple of Ramses II, Abu Simbel
stops.includedNote: Admission to both temples is included in the Base + Entrance Fees and Base + Entrance Fees & Lunch tiers, not in the Base package.

stops.title: The Small Temple of Nefertari and Hathor
stops.text: Roughly a hundred metres to the north, it is the only Egyptian temple in which a queen's statues are carved at the same scale as the pharaoh's, and its reliefs include some of the best-preserved colour in any Nubian monument. Your guide moves you through both temples in sequence; plan for two to two and a half hours on site.
sites: Small Temple of Nefertari and Hathor, Abu Simbel

stops.title: Drive back to Aswan
stops.text: After the temples you return to your vehicle for the drive back north. Arrival in Aswan is typically late afternoon, depending on departure time and any stops along the road.
